esimgg-estonia-372-number.title: [Global] eSIM.GG: an Estonian +372 number for EUR 2.99, no monthly fee, stays alive with one use a year
esimgg-estonia-372-number.highlight: EUR 2.99 buys an eSIM with a +372 Estonian number, no monthly fee and a balance that never expires; one qualifying use within 365 days renews it. In mainland China it roams on China Unicom: EUR 4.7 per GB and free incoming SMS, but no voice calls there
esimgg-estonia-372-number.regions: [Global] An Estonian +372 number usable in 154+ countries; mainland roaming runs on China Unicom with no in-country voice
esimgg-estonia-372-number.content: Known as the turtle card: a prepaid eSIM with an Estonian +372 number that receives texts, takes calls and buys roaming data, priced at €2.99 for the number itself with no monthly fee and credit that never expires. It stays alive with any activity within 365 days — data, a text, a call, a top-up or a successful network connection — which restarts the year, while 365 days of nothing can reclaim the number (a change to balance-based keeping is announced). Rates as of 21 November 2026: data from €0.88 a GB in most of Europe and Asia, a 10GB pack across 42 countries for €9 including China, the US, UK, EU, Malaysia and Thailand, and in mainland China €4.7 a GB with free incoming texts, €0.24 outgoing and no voice; the site says ChatGPT and TikTok work. Tests around 30 yuan to start got WhatsApp codes on an iPhone after about 24 hours via eSTK, Telegram accepts some ranges, and the first connection needs about a day of technical updating.
esimgg-estonia-372-number.conditions: Buy at esim.gg from €2.99 for a number (some need a deposit); no monthly fee or real-name check, with an install code right after payment; any activity within 365 days keeps it; an unlocked eSIM phone or an eSTK or eSIM.me; third-party code delivery is not guaranteed.
steps: Open esim.gg and pick a +372 number; numbers marked in red need 24 hours to 3 days before SMS works
After payment take the install code and write it to the phone's native eSIM or an external eUICC
Wait about 24 hours for provisioning, then send a test SMS from the line's diagnostics page
Put the expiry date in a calendar and do one qualifying activity a month early each year
esimgg-estonia-372-number.risk: The EUR 2.99 does not include a first balance, so real opening cost is about CNY 30, and every year needs a small paid activity. The vendor has announced moving from activity-based to balance-based keep-alive, so the yearly cost must be recalculated once that lands. Third-party codes are not guaranteed and one working platform proves nothing for others. New lines need 24 hours to 3 days of provisioning. Voice is unavailable in mainland China and outgoing SMS costs EUR 0.24. The upstream operator can raise prices or shut the service down, with 90 days' notice at best.
esimgg-estonia-372-number.source: eSIM.GG official home page and world coverage and rate pages (updated 2026-11-21: EUR 2.99 number, data from 0.88 per GB, 10GB for 42 countries at EUR 9, China data EUR 4.7 per GB with free incoming SMS and EUR 0.24 outgoing, 145 countries covered) plus the official FAQ and terms (365-day qualifying activity, clause 8 on upstream operator changes) plus nbvil blog purchase test on 2026-10-16 (EUR 2.99, WhatsApp code after about 24 hours, eSTKme Plus+ works) plus WithGoddess test on 2026-10-15 (Telegram codes on listed number ranges, about CNY 30 to open)

clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.title: [Hong Kong] Club SIM: a +852 number with no monthly fee, kept alive by a HKD 15 pass each year (free incoming SMS in the mainland)
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.highlight: csl's build-your-own prepaid card: no monthly fee and a free eSIM ordered online, with a +852 number once the first order reaches HKD 50; after that one HKD 15 Asia pass within 365 days adds another year, and mainland China receives SMS free
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.regions: [HK] A +852 number on csl up to 4.5G at 42Mbps; incoming texts are free worldwide
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.content: A build-your-own prepaid card from csl: order an eSIM online without using a SIM slot, pay no monthly fee and keep the number under Hong Kong stored-value rules, where any purchase within 365 days of the last one extends validity by another year. The old HK$6 SMS pack retired on 30 June 2026 with no return planned, leaving the HK$15 24-hour Asia roaming pass as the cheapest renewal, so a year of upkeep rose from HK$6 to HK$15. New cards need a first order of HK$50 in total, with eSIM free, and the usual trick is HK$38 of mainland and Macau data for 90 days plus the HK$15 Asia pass, HK$53 on one card. Incoming texts are free worldwide, so codes arrive in the mainland without roaming; there are no calls or outgoing texts, and data needs the roaming packs (1GB for HK$38 or 3GB for HK$88 in the mainland and Macau, both 90 days). Real-name registration takes a passport or travel permit, not a mainland ID, photographed in the app, and eSIM and physical SIM can swap in the app (HK$40 per extra swap within a year).
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.conditions: Order an eSIM online with a first order of HK$50+ (eSIM issuance free); local service needs real-name registration with a passport or permit, not a mainland ID, and without it there are no calls or texts; keep it by buying any pack within 365 days, now from the HK$15 Asia pass; packs carry their own validity (90 days) separate from the number; the buffer after expiry is short.
steps: On clubsim.com.hk choose an eSIM and packs totalling at least HKD 50, for example mainland and Macao 1GB at HKD 38 plus the HKD 15 Asia pass
Install the QR code from the confirmation email on a native eSIM phone or an external eUICC
Open the Club SIM app and register with a passport or mainland travel permit, then wait for approval
Note the last pack date plus 365 days in a calendar and buy a HKD 15 pass before it comes round
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.risk: Forgetting the yearly renewal loses the number for good, and every bank or platform tied to it must be changed. The HKD 6 era is over and the yearly cost is now HKD 15. In the mainland it only receives SMS, with no calls or outgoing messages, and data is a separate purchase. Registration is mandatory and a mainland ID is not accepted, so without a passport or travel permit the card is out of reach, and spot checks can follow. Hong Kong numbers have a poor record on AI platforms such as ChatGPT. Packs are non-refundable once ordered.
clubsim-hk-prepaid-number.source: Club SIM official site (clubsim.com.hk checked 2026-11-22: build-your-own prepaid, HKD 15 Asia 24-hour pass, mainland and Macao roaming HKD 38 for 1GB and HKD 88 for 3GB, both 90 days, free eSIM) plus SimDirs Club Sim review (rechecked 2026-11-12: keep-alive rule, HKD 50 first order, registration required for Hong Kong service) plus NomadInit Club SIM guide (2026-08-14: HKD 6 SMS pack withdrawn on 2026-06-30) plus NodeSeek post-1064567 (2026-11-19: HKD 53 order, blank-card install, mainland SMS test) plus the Naixi forum thread 12923 (2026-06-30 withdrawal discussion)

hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.title: [Hong Kong] haha SIM: HKD 50 card with HKD 50 credit, no monthly fee, kept alive by a HKD 10 top-up a year (physical SIM)
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.highlight: A 3HK prepaid card sold by Fortress: HKD 50 for the card with HKD 50 of credit inside, no monthly fee, and free incoming SMS in the mainland; one HKD 10 top-up a year in the app keeps the +852 number for another 365 days, and only Hong Kong local service needs registration
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.regions: [HK] A +852 number on 3HK, physical SIM only (no eSIM yet); incoming texts free on mainland roaming
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.content: A recyclable travel prepaid card from Hutchison (3HK) sold through Fortress: typically HK$50 with HK$50 of credit inside, so the card is effectively free, and it must be first inserted before the last-activation date printed on the pack. The number lasts 365 days, extended another 365 by a top-up of HK$10+ in the haha TRAVEL app or on 3HK's top-up page every 12 months; buying data packs does not keep it alive, the app's minimum is often HK$20, so a HK$10 top-up goes through 3HK's site (which takes WeChat Pay and Alipay from the mainland). Within 14 days of expiry a restart can be requested but is not guaranteed and needs new real-name registration. On mainland roaming incoming texts are free while sending costs HK$3.5, answering HK$8 a minute, calls to Hong Kong HK$8 and to the mainland HK$6, and data comes from mainland day passes (often HK$10 a day, throttled after about 500MB). Real-name registration applies only to Hong Kong local service, not to plain roaming codes.
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.conditions: Buy the physical card at Fortress or 3HK (HK$50 with HK$50 credit) and insert it before the last-activation date; top up HK$10+ every 12 months, as data packs do not count; real-name only for Hong Kong service; no eSIM from the operator, so the phone needs an unlocked physical slot; numbers are assigned at random.
steps: Buy a haha SIM from Fortress and check the last activation date on the box
Turn Wi-Fi off, insert the card in slot one with automatic network selection, and read the +852 number in the activation SMS
Log into haha TRAVEL with the number and ICCID, then screenshot the balance and expiry date
Top up at least HKD 10 before the expiry date each year, using the 3HK page for an exact HKD 10, and confirm the new date
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.risk: Physical SIM only, with no eSIM, and the last activation date on the box is easy to miss. Keeping the number depends on a top-up, data packs do not count, and the app often starts at HKD 20, so overpaying is common. After 14 days past expiry the number cannot be recovered. In the mainland everything runs on roaming and calls and SMS are expensive. Numbers are random and cannot be chosen, and platforms such as Telegram and Google reject them often. Hong Kong local service needs registration, so an unregistered card is roaming-only.
hahasim-hk-prepaid-number.source: Fortress haha SIM product page and 3HK prepaid terms (checked 2026-11: HKD 50 with HKD 50 credit, 365 days from activation, top-up of at least HKD 10 extends it, data packs do not, registration only for Hong Kong service) plus the UGO EARN hahaSIM guide (2026-09-26, checked against the Fortress site: top-up rather than data pack, HKD 10 mainland day pass, code tests) plus the Linnainai guide (2026-11-01: 14-day limit, unregistered scope) plus the hokada guide (2026-11-10) plus Shuziyoumin hahaSIM introduction (updated 2026-06-18: app minimum HKD 20, official page allows HKD 10)

aws-quick-free-plus-trial.title: [Global] AWS Quick: $0 free plan forever, plus an automatic 30-day Plus trial (no AWS account, no card)
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.highlight: Sign up at aws.amazon.com/quick with any personal email or a Google / Apple / GitHub / Amazon account and you get the $0 single-user Free plan right away: 1GB index storage, AI chat, Research reports, Spaces, custom agents, Flows and one-prompt web apps, with Slack / M365 / Google / QuickBooks connectors. Every new signup also starts a 30-day Plus trial ($25 a month normally) — no AWS account and no credit card at any point.
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.regions: [Global] Sign up at aws.amazon.com/quick with an email or Google, Apple, GitHub or Amazon account; no AWS account or card
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.content: At aws.amazon.com/quick choose Sign up for free and register with any email or a Google, Apple, GitHub or Amazon account: enter the email, take the six-digit code, set a password (8+ characters with upper and lower case, a number and a symbol) and it opens in about a minute, with an AWS account created behind the scenes that you never touch and no card. The free plan is $0 long-term: one user, 1GB of index storage, AI chat, Quick Research reports with citations, Spaces, custom chat agents, Quick Flows automation and one-line web apps, connecting to Slack, Microsoft 365, Google and QuickBooks. Signup automatically includes a 30-day Plus trial (nothing to claim, no card): shared Spaces, browser and Microsoft 365 extensions, user management and central billing, 10GB per seat and up to 10 team members; Plus normally costs $25 a seat a month ($20 annually). No tier trains models on your data.
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.conditions: The 30-day Plus trial is only for new aws.amazon.com/quick accounts (enterprise accounts opened in the AWS console are different); upgrading to Plus needs contact details, a four-digit SMS check and a card, then bills monthly; the free plan is single-user with 1GB of index storage and $5/GB a month beyond; at trial end the official wording is continue with Plus or return to Free, without stating a default.
steps: Open aws.amazon.com/quick and choose Sign up for free
Register with an email (or Google / Apple / GitHub / Amazon), enter the 6-digit email code and set a password that meets the rules
The account provisions in about a minute; download the macOS desktop app or continue on the web, then skip or pick a work focus
During the trial, go to your avatar → Manage account → Plan and billing to see the current plan, days remaining and estimated charges
To keep the free plan, choose Manage plan → Free within the 30 days; continuing on Plus is the only step that needs details, phone verification and a card
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.risk: No card is taken at signup, so an untouched account cannot be charged; upgrading to Plus is what requires a card, then $25 per user per month renews automatically ($20 on annual billing, which cannot be cancelled mid-term). The billing settings let you enable overages, which start charging beyond your monthly agent hours and 1GB of index storage ($5/GB/month) — leave them off. Two official pages disagree, so check Manage plan after signing in: the pricing comparison marks the desktop app as available on Free, while the FAQ says the desktop app is for Plus, Professional and Enterprise (including the trial); the browser and Microsoft 365 extensions are likewise blank for Free in the table but listed as included in the FAQ. Neither page publishes the monthly agent-hour allowance for Free or Plus (only Enterprise gets 1 / 8 / 18 hours), so heavy use may hit a cap quickly — marked unverified. AWS does not say whether signing up again can bring the trial back, so it is understood as one trial per new account (marked unverified).
aws-quick-free-plus-trial.source: AWS Quick site and pricing page (fetched 2026-11-22), the official Quick FAQ (original wording on the free plan and trial), AWS docs "Signing up at aws.com/quick" and "Plan and billing for AWS Quick Free, Plus, and Max accounts", and the AWS what's-new post of 2026-04-28 announcing the Free and Plus plans

claude-max-monthly-api-credits.title: [Global] Claude Max and Ultra subscriptions now include monthly API credits: $100 on Max, $200 on Ultra, $20–$100 per Team seat (pool capped at $500 a month)
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.highlight: Anthropic folded API credits into its subscriptions: Max ($100/mo) grants $100 of Claude API credit a month, Ultra ($200/mo) grants $200, and Team grants $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat pooled into one balance capped at $500 a month. Link a Claude Console organization from claude.ai and build with it without adding a card.
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.regions: [Global] An active Max, Ultra or Team plan is enough; credits refresh each billing cycle; Free, Pro and Enterprise excluded
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.content: Since 7 October 2026 Max ($100 a month) includes $100 of Claude API credit a month and Ultra ($200) includes $200; Team pools per seat (Standard $20, Premium $100) into one pot capped at $500 per organization a month, with discounted nonprofit and research Team plans on the same terms. Free, Pro and Enterprise are out. In claude.ai open Settings > Billing (organization billing for Team), choose API credits then Link organization and link a Claude Console organization; one plan per organization and one organization per plan, with support needed to change a wrong link. The credit covers the Claude API (Messages and Batches), Playground, Managed Agents and the Agent SDK, including claude -p run with the organization's key, but not interactive Claude Code, plan extra usage or Claude on Bedrock, Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry; it refreshes each cycle without rollover, is shared by the organization's API keys and is spent before purchased credit. Community tests (linux.do, 8 October 2026) confirm Max 5x claims $100, Max 20x $200 and a Team owner can claim, while some app-store subscribers never see the card.
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.conditions: An active plan in good standing for seven days at the eligible tier; link the Console organization from claude.ai Settings > Billing (organization billing for Team), as the claimer needs the Owner, Admin or Billing role; one organization per plan and one plan per organization; credits refresh each cycle without rollover; coverage is the Claude API, Playground, Managed Agents and Agent SDK but not interactive Claude Code or plan extra usage; no card is needed on the Claude Platform.
steps: Confirm you are on Max or Ultra (or are a Team owner) and have been for seven days
Create a Claude Console organization at platform.claude.com, or reuse one, signing in with the same email as claude.ai
Back on claude.ai, open Settings > Billing > API credits > Link organization and confirm
Check the amount and expiry on the Console billing page
Call the Claude API with that organization's key; after the credit runs out it continues from your own balance or auto-reload
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.risk: It is a subscription perk, so you pay $100 a month or more first; the credit is not cash, cannot be withdrawn and expires each cycle; it does not cover Claude Code in the terminal or IDE, so it will not replace a Claude Code budget; only one Console organization can be linked, and fixing a mistake needs support; some Google Play and App Store subscribers report the claim card never appearing; the rollout is still gradual, so a fresh seven-day subscription may not show the entry yet.
claude-max-monthly-api-credits.source: Anthropic Help Center 'Monthly API credits for Max, Ultra, and Team plans' (read 22 November 2026: amounts, seven-day rule, linking flow, coverage) + claude.com/pricing (Max $100, Ultra $200, monthly API credit noted) + linux.do community reports (8 October 2026)

google-antigravity-science-free.title: [Global] Google Antigravity for science: 10,000 researchers get the highest usage tier free for six months, with Gemini 4 Argon
google-antigravity-science-free.highlight: At the Gemini 4 Argon launch Google offered 10,000 scientists six months of Antigravity's highest usage tier plus Gemini 4 Argon at no cost. The Google account used to submit the interest form is the one upgraded, personal Gmail or university Workspace alike, with rolling weekly review since 13 October.
google-antigravity-science-free.regions: [Global] Non-commercial researchers at universities, degree-granting institutes, non-profits and national labs
google-antigravity-science-free.value: 6 months of the top usage tier
google-antigravity-science-free.content: Up to 10,000 researchers get six months of Antigravity's highest usage tier plus Gemini 4 Argon, free; Argon normally needs Google AI Ultra at $249.99 a month, so the grant is worth half a year of Ultra-level agent usage. Apply through the interest form at antigravity.google/use-cases/science while signed in to the Google account you want upgraded, giving your institution, institutional email, a public lab or personal page, an ORCID or Google Scholar profile, and a 6-12 month research summary that must not be confidential or proprietary. Review is weekly and capacity-limited: from 13 October 2026 more than 27,000 applications arrived, about 3,000 were granted first and unsuccessful applicants are not told. Once in, install the Science plugin from the Customizations market to query AlphaGenome, AlphaFold Database, UniProt, PubChem, ChEMBL and 30+ life-science databases; fields run beyond biology to medicine, chemistry and materials, physics and fusion, quantum, climate, neuroscience, maths, computer science, engineering, social science, agriculture and economics, as long as the work is non-commercial.
google-antigravity-science-free.conditions: Non-commercial research only; applicants must be staff or students at a university, degree-granting institute, non-profit research institute or national lab (faculty, postdocs, researchers, PhD and master's students; no option for undergraduates); an ORCID or Google Scholar profile is required; the summary must not contain confidential or unpublished data; capped at 10,000 places, reviewed on a rolling basis with only successful applicants contacted; only the Google account used on the form is upgraded.
steps: Sign in with the Google account you want upgraded at antigravity.google/use-cases/science
Click Apply for free access and fill in institution, institutional email and a public page
Add an ORCID or Google Scholar link and a 6-12 month research summary
Submit and wait for rolling review; selected applicants are notified and the account is upgraded
Install the Science plugin from Antigravity's Customizations marketplace
google-antigravity-science-free.risk: The 10,000 places are a ceiling, not a promise: Google reported about 3,000 admitted from over 27,000 applications by 10 November, fewer than one in nine; the top tier has no published quota, so heavy multi-agent work may still hit limits; the programme says nothing about what happens after six months, so do not rest a project on it; the research summary is stored by Google, so keep it non-confidential; the upgrade belongs to the individual account, not an institution.
google-antigravity-science-free.source: Google Antigravity science use-case page (read 22 November 2026: 10,000 scientists, highest usage tier and Gemini 4 Argon free) + Google Gemini for Science page + Google's 13 October 2026 announcement and press checks (six months, applications open, 27,000 applications and about 3,000 admitted by 10 November) + linux.do repost (21 November 2026)

lovable-linkedin-premium-year.title: [US/UK/CA/AU] Lovable x LinkedIn Premium: a year of Pro Lite plus a one-time 300 credits
lovable-linkedin-premium-year.highlight: An official LinkedIn and Lovable perk: paying LinkedIn Premium members whose account is in the US, UK, Canada or Australia can claim a year of Lovable Pro Lite, with every Pro feature and 5 bonus credits a day, plus a one-time 300 credits from LinkedIn's Premium perks page. The Lovable side must be a new or free workspace.
lovable-linkedin-premium-year.regions: [US/UK/CA/AU] LinkedIn account in the US, UK, Canada or Australia with a paid Premium plan
lovable-linkedin-premium-year.content: Paid LinkedIn Premium members whose account is in the US, UK, Canada or Australia can open the Lovable card on LinkedIn's Premium perks page and claim 12 months of Lovable Pro Lite plus a one-time 300 credits on activation. Pro Lite includes every standard Pro feature but only 5 bonus credits a day and no monthly allowance, so heavy work still needs bought credits. Claim through LinkedIn's official path in a desktop browser (iOS cannot redeem), on the primary account only; Premium Company Page subscribers do not count and free trials must convert with a first payment. The Lovable side must be a new or free workspace, not an existing paid plan; codes are single-use and non-transferable. Other regions are described as rolling out — whether you can claim depends on the card appearing in your perks page.
lovable-linkedin-premium-year.conditions: A paid LinkedIn Premium subscription (trials must convert with a first payment) with the account in the US, UK, Canada or Australia; claim from the LinkedIn Premium perks page, not on an iOS device; primary accounts only, Premium Company Page subscribers excluded; a new or free Lovable workspace, not an existing paid plan; codes are single-use and non-transferable.
steps: Sign in to LinkedIn in a desktop browser and confirm Premium is an active paid plan
Open the Premium perks page, find the Lovable card and follow it
Continue to Lovable and sign in to or create a workspace that is not already paid
Confirm activation; 300 credits land once and the Pro Lite term appears in the account
Put the end date in a calendar so the workspace does not quietly fall back to Free
lovable-linkedin-premium-year.risk: You must already pay for LinkedIn Premium, so it is not free in cash terms; only LinkedIn accounts in the US, UK, Canada and Australia are accepted for now, so check that the card exists in your perks page; Lovable only accepts a new or free workspace, so existing paid accounts cannot claim; Pro Lite has no monthly credits, only 5 a day, which runs out fast; the offer can change, so confirm before redeeming.

articul8-bivia-1b-tokens.content: Intel-backed Articul8 launched Bivia, a decision model that reads text, images, documents, code, signals and audio or video and returns a structured verdict in one of nine decision types (Choice, Boolean, Score, Set, Span, Ground, Extract, Data science and others) with a real confidence score, and allow_abstain lets it decline when evidence is thin. Output tokens are free and input costs $0.042 per million, suiting routing, classification and yes/no calls at volume so larger models save capacity for code and long writing. The launch gives the first 10,000 users up to 1 billion tokens with no subscription via Claim yours at articul8.ai/bivia, worth about $42 at input pricing. It is not a chat model and only returns fixed-shape verdicts.
articul8-bivia-1b-tokens.conditions: Claim at signup with no subscription per the official terms; first 10,000 users only, first come; the official wording is up to 1 billion tokens and the actual grant shows in the account; validity and deadline are unpublished (community reports about 90 days); credit covers Articul8 and Bivia inference only, with overage at $0.042 per million input tokens and nothing for output.

Finish signup on the Articul8 platform, create an API key and check the early-adopter balance
Connect it with pip install bivia, the npm package, or the MCP server in Claude Code or Cursor
Validate decision quality and latency on small jobs before putting it in a pipeline

The dormant-account fee starts 183 days after the last transaction and keeps charging monthly. Crypto funding carries blockchain and compliance risk, large amounts can trigger source-of-funds questions, and this is not a place to park savings. Using the GB IBAN to activate Wise is a user claim that Wise has never promised to accept. The card is not launched, so any claim that it can be opened now is false or third-party. The app is not in the mainland China App Store and switching store regions carries its own risk; when verifying with an ID card, a polyphonic surname is romanised from the document and can end up differently from what you expect, in which case a passport is the alternative.

Nodaroo, a small host launched in November 2026 at nodaroo.com with machines in Frankfurt and Mumbai, released free containers on 22 November: sign in to free.nodaroo.com with Discord for one box with 200% shared CPU, 6GB of RAM, 50GB of NVMe, one slot and a German node, without a card or KYC. Entry is Discord-only, with OAuth scopes identify, email and guilds.join that also join its server, and an invite link adds 100 points, 25 to the referrer, for more CPU, RAM, disk and slots. Its Discord lists recruitment tiers: Light at 18 people or 300 views for 24GB and four cores, Premium at 25 or 600 for 32GB and six, and Extreme at 35 or 1,000 for 48GB and eight. Technically it is a container panel, Heliactyl in front and Pterodactyl behind, not a bare KVM: no root or native SSH, only a web console and SFTP on 2022, ports limited to those assigned, no Docker-in-Docker and 200% CPU as a shared allowance. By 23 November the panel returned an error asking to retry or contact support, with the community reporting signup and creation failures.
nodaroo-free-container-host.conditions: Archived and ended: Discord sign-in with no card or KYC; one free workspace per new account; the site link opens the basic tier while invites add 100 points; 200% shared CPU, 6GB, 50GB NVMe, one slot, German node; a container rather than KVM without root or native SSH and with panel-assigned ports only; the panel errored on 23 November 2026.

Keep it to tests, bots and cron jobs, back up anything important elsewhere and never make it the only production environment
nodaroo-free-container-host.risk: Archived as expired: on 23 November 2026 the user's own test got "Something went wrong. Please retry or contact Nodaroo support" from the panel, and NodeLoc replies at the same time said "not working now" and reported the China region failing, so do not treat it as a usable free machine. Historic risks remain: a very new host from November 2026 whose free resources can be reclaimed or shut down at any moment, so back up important data and never make it the only production environment; a container cannot run Docker, has no root or SSH, no dedicated public IPv4 and only panel-assigned ports; the 200% CPU is a shared allowance throttled under fair use; the referral upgrade tiers were a limited-time campaign, so do not recruit people for them, and this site never carries invite links. plugsky-free-llm-api.value: Free API (100 requests / 50,000 tokens a day for new accounts)
plugsky-free-llm-api.content: The Free plan costs $0, needs no card and includes two API keys for plugsky-micro and plugsky-lite, 30B total parameters with about 3B active and a per-request ceiling of 32K input and 2K output. The endpoint is fully OpenAI-compatible at https://plugsky.com/v1 (api.plugsky.com/v1 also answers) with streaming, tool calling and JSON mode. Allowances differ by account age: accounts created from 2 November 2026 get 100 requests and 50,000 tokens a day with one concurrent request, while earlier accounts keep 500 requests and 250,000 tokens with two until the provider finishes migrating them. Both are limited to 30 RPM, reset at 00:00 UTC and return 429 when exhausted. The privacy policy states prompts and completions are not used to train models.
plugsky-free-llm-api.conditions: The free tier needs no card; create a key and call it. New accounts get 100 requests and 50,000 tokens a day with one concurrent request, older ones 500 requests and 250,000 tokens with two. Both are capped at 30 RPM and at 32K input and 2K output per request, and the free tier only exposes micro and lite.
steps: Sign up at plugsky.com with an email (Google sign-in also works) and open Dashboard then API keys
Create a key and set your client's base_url to https://plugsky.com/v1
Send one test request each to plugsky-micro and plugsky-lite
Watch daily usage in the Dashboard or GET /v1/plugsky/usage, keeping 30 RPM and the daily cap in mind
plugsky-free-llm-api.risk: New accounts get a fifth of the older allowance and the provider gives no date for finishing the migration. The free tier only serves 30B-class micro and lite, so don't treat it as a frontier model; 32K input and 2K output per request will truncate long documents and long code. The homepage figures such as 35M daily calls cover paid plans, and the free tier carries no SLA. The privacy policy says free-tier failover can route through third-party free providers such as OpenRouter, Groq and LLM7, which may keep short-lived anti-abuse logs but may not train on them. The site is new and its allowances and terms can change at any time.
plugsky-free-llm-api.source: Plugsky official pricing page (read 2026-11-23: Free $0, no card, new accounts 100 requests / 50,000 tokens / 1 concurrent, older 500 / 250,000 / 2, 30 RPM, 32K input / 2K output) + official FAQ and privacy policy (no training, anti-abuse logs on free-tier failover) + official docs (base_url) + live GET /v1/models returning 39 models with micro and lite on the free tier (2026-11-23)

The OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://chat.merkium.nl/api/v1 allows 30 requests a minute, strictly one every two seconds per key.
merkium-free-llm-api.regions: [Global] Sign up with an email, no card needed; the site lists no country restriction
merkium-free-llm-api.value: Free API (7 models at $0 permanently, no daily cap)
merkium-free-llm-api.content: ganymede-1.1 (780B MoE with 20B active, 1M context, 16,384 output, tool calling and streaming) plus pluto-1.2-flash and pro, pluto-1.1-flash and pro, and ceres-1.0 and pro are all free permanently; the site states this is not a trial, never expires and needs no credit card. The API is OpenAI-compatible at https://chat.merkium.nl/api/v1 and keys are free in the Console at chat.merkium.nl. Each key is limited to 30 requests a minute, enforced as one request every two seconds, with a 429 and Retry-After when exceeded, and no daily cap is published. The other six models publish output limits of 900 to 4,096 tokens but no context window. The provider says future models may be paid while these seven stay free, and that conversations are not used for training.
merkium-free-llm-api.conditions: Register with an email and create a free key in the Console; no card. Each key allows 30 requests a minute with at least two seconds between requests, and over-limit calls return 429. No daily cap is published. Only ganymede-1.1 publishes a 1M context and 16K output; the other models publish no context window. Future models may charge.
steps: Register at chat.merkium.nl and sign in
Open the API tab of the Console, create a key and store it in an environment variable
Point an OpenAI-compatible client's base_url at https://chat.merkium.nl/api/v1
Send a test request to ganymede-1.1 and space scripted calls two seconds apart to avoid 429
merkium-free-llm-api.risk: This is a one-person project in the Netherlands (Afonso Faro, not yet a registered company) with no SLA and no paid fallback, so use it for experiments and personal projects rather than production. Only ganymede-1.1 publishes a context window, so don't plan long documents around the others. The system card admits weaker Chinese than English and misses details in very long inputs, and its evaluations are internal. The hard two-second spacing means queuing your own calls, so it is unsuitable for concurrent workloads. The seven models are promised free, but new ones may charge. The docs were last verified on 20 October 2026, so read GET /models for the live list; direct access from mainland China is untested.
merkium-free-llm-api.source: Merkium official pricing docs (read 2026-11-23: 7 models free permanently, no card, 30 requests a minute / one every two seconds, base_url) + rate-limit and model docs (only ganymede-1.1 publishes a 1M context and 16,384 output) + Ganymede 1.1 system card and privacy policy (no training, one-person project) + live GET /api/v1/models returning 401 invalid_api_key (endpoint up, key required, 2026-11-23)

The platform creates a paper contest account marked CME with $25,000 virtual funds and live data

gnoland-gnome-tavern-hackathon.highlight: Deploy anything that runs on the Gno.land testnet, 16 projects share $20,000 paid in GNOT, and winners can match their prize by keeping the project alive
gnoland-gnome-tavern-hackathon.content: There is no required theme: a realm, dApp, developer tool or small demo that is deployed and working on the Gno.land testnet counts, submitted with a public repository, README, demo video and deployment link. Write a realm, dApp or tool in Gno and deploy it to the testnet using free faucet funds
Prepare the public repository, README and a demo video under three minutes, then submit the deployment link
After winners are announced on 21 December, complete KYC to receive the GNOT payout
gnoland-gnome-tavern-hackathon.risk: Prizes are paid in GNOT at market price, so the dollar value moves with the token; the retention prize is not guaranteed and needs continued development, usage and adoption; a winner who misses the 22 December KYC deadline delays payment; the organiser may adjust dates and award counts.

immunefi-base-everest-audit-comp.regions: [Global] Online audit, KYC required; sanctioned regions excluded

Build the pinned local Everest devnet or a mainnet fork and start reviewing the in-scope code
Write a runnable PoC for any valid bug and submit the report on the platform
Follow triage and fixes, then complete KYC within 7 days of being asked to receive USDC
immunefi-base-everest-audit-comp.risk: $250,000 is the ceiling when a Critical is found, and only valid, reproducible bugs pay; reports and results are published and scope follows the pinned commit; KYC not submitted within 7 days can forfeit the reward.

reactive-omni-buildathon.content: Reactive Omni produces roughly one-second blocks, and this buildathon is about what that speed makes possible. Three tracks: Every Second Counts for arbitrage, stop-loss and take-profit work on Unichain or Base Sepolia ($2,000 first, $250 runner-up), Set It and Forget It for personal automations ($2,000/$250), and Reactive Meets AI, where the model must sit in the running loop rather than only helping write code ($1,000). Entries need a public repository, deployed contract addresses, transaction hashes covering the full event-to-callback loop and a demo video under three minutes; the work must be built during the event, and testnet REACT comes free from the official faucet.
reactive-omni-buildathon.conditions: Solo or team, no contract experience needed; repositories must be public and open source at submission; work must be built between 5 November and 5 December; use timestamps rather than block counts on Base Sepolia.
steps: Register on the DoraHacks page, pick a track and read its network and submission rules
Get testnet REACT from the Lasna faucet and deploy a reactive contract following the docs
Run the full origin-event to callback loop and record the transaction hashes
Submit the public repository, deployed addresses and a demo video under three minutes before 5 December 20:00 UTC
reactive-omni-buildathon.risk: Prizes are paid in REACT at market price; only five prizes exist and the Reactive team judges subjectively; entries without a deployment or real callback transactions are not scored.

Confirm the $1,000 simulated balance and the locked starting baseline
Trade the approved competition markets by hand or through the API, a bot or an AI agent
After 31 December, wait for performance verification and complete the prize claim checks

Pick Midterms markets that resolve before 30 November and place Ooms trades

rikkahub-android-llm-client.title: [Global] RikkaHub: a free, open-source Android LLM client with switchable providers (AGPL-3.0)
rikkahub-android-llm-client.highlight: A native Android chat client: plug in your own models, Material 3 throughout, plus a root-free Linux workspace and phone control. 9,130 stars, no ads, no in-app purchases, AGPL-3.0 source.
rikkahub-android-llm-client.regions: [Global] Works on any Android 8.0+ phone; the release APK is arm64-v8a only; no regional restriction
rikkahub-android-llm-client.value: Completely free (open source under AGPL-3.0, no ads, no in-app purchases)
rikkahub-android-llm-client.content: A native Android LLM client written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (AGPL-3.0, 9,130 stars on 2026-11-23). v3.3.1 shipped on 2026-11-21: the site and GitHub Releases serve a 15.69 MB arm64-v8a APK, and Google Play lists the same app with 10,000+ downloads and 4.6 stars. Connect OpenAI, Google, Anthropic or any compatible base URL, and move provider setups between phones by QR code; it also ships a root-free proot Linux workspace, Phone Use that taps your phone through the accessibility service, MCP and Skills, web search, and SillyTavern character card import. No in-app purchases and no ads; funded by donations.
rikkahub-android-llm-client.conditions: Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26); the official APK is arm64-v8a only, and the Play build cannot self-update; no bundled model quota, so bring your own API key or relay, and the built-in free fallback is strictly rate-limited; AGPL-3.0 obliges anyone redistributing a modified build to publish its source.
steps: Install only from rikka-ai.com/download, GitHub Releases or Google Play (the README warns that outside forks may ask for excessive permissions)
Open Settings, then Providers, add OpenAI, Google, Anthropic or a custom base URL with your key; a QR code can import a provider setup
Start a chat and pick a model (providers are switchable and thinking depth adjustable); for web search, add an Exa or Tavily key in the search settings
Turn on the workspace (root-free proot Linux with a terminal) or Phone Use (accessibility access) when you want it to act, starting with low-risk tasks
rikkahub-android-llm-client.risk: The README warns that many forks of RikkaHub exist and that fork problems are unrelated to the project, and a fork may leak data or request extra permissions, so install only from the official site, GitHub Releases or Play. Model and search usage is on your own bill, and the built-in free fallback is heavily rate-limited, so do not plan on it long term. Phone Use needs the accessibility service, which effectively hands the phone to the AI, so keep payment apps out of it at first. The project accepts no pull requests and had 310 open issues when checked, and 3.3.1 still fixed regressions (DeepSeek import crashing on Android 9 and 10, update downloads failing with a VPN on). AGPL-3.0 obliges anyone distributing a modified build to publish its source.
rikkahub-android-llm-client.source: GitHub rikkahub/rikkahub (read 2026-11-23: 9,130 stars, 933 forks, AGPL-3.0, last push 2026-11-21) + official site rikka-ai.com/download (v3.3.1, 2026-11-21, 15.69 MB APK) + Google Play me.rerere.rikkahub (10,000+ downloads, 4.6 stars, updated 2026-11-21) + repository strings.xml and app/build.gradle.kts (minSdk 26, no Play Billing dependency, built-in free fallback provider)

simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.title: [Global] SIMHub: manage eSIM cards through a reader and call or text over Wi-Fi Calling, free sideload on iOS, macOS and Android
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.highlight: Manage eSIM profiles through a card reader and call or text over Wi-Fi Calling on iOS, macOS and Android, now free to sideload from GitHub. The iOS build left the App Store on 7 Oct 2026, so the developer posts IPA, APK and macOS packages in its place; the card ledger and expiry reminders work without any reader.
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.regions: [Global] Distributed online with no regional restriction
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.content: A SIM and eSIM card manager for iOS/iPadOS 17+, macOS 14+ and Android 8+. With a USB CCID reader (USB OTG on Android) or a 9eSIM B0/B1 Bluetooth reader attached, it reads the EID and ICCID, enables, disables, renames and deletes profiles, downloads new ones from a QR code or activation code, and handles pending card notifications; 5ber, Xesim, eSTK, 9eSIM and multi-chip cards such as eSTK.me Max are supported. A card in the reader can place and take calls and send and receive SMS over IKEv2/IPsec and IMS, and a reader or module on a Mac or NAS can be lent to an iPhone over the local network or Tailscale. Pricing: SIMHub X still sells for $2.99 on Google Play with no ads and no in-app purchases listed; the iOS build has been off the App Store since 7 Oct 2026 pending an appeal, and the developer now offers a 29.3 IPA, a 29.22 macOS package and a 23.1 APK free on GitHub.
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.conditions: Reader and Wi-Fi Calling features need a compatible CCID reader (USB OTG on Android) or a 9eSIM B0/B1 Bluetooth reader plus a writable eSIM card such as eSTK, 9eSIM, 5ber or Xesim, and the carrier must have Wi-Fi Calling enabled; iOS 17+ is required (older devices must use SIMKit); a free Apple ID signature expires every 7 days and has to be refreshed.
steps: Open the Releases page of the maow318/simhubforum repository on GitHub and download the package for your platform: SIMHub-29.3.ipa for iOS/iPadOS, SIMHub-macOS-29.22.zip for macOS, SIMHub-Android-23.1.apk for Android
On iOS, re-sign the IPA with your own Apple ID using AltStore, Sideloadly or a similar tool and install it; a free Apple ID needs re-signing every 7 days, and app data stays on the device
On macOS, unzip it, move SIMHub.app to Applications and open it (it is notarized); on Android, allow installing unknown apps and open the APK, with no re-signing needed

Attach a reader, read the EID and profile list, then download a new profile by scanning a QR code or entering an activation code; for Wi-Fi Calling pick the carrier profile and test with a number already on the card
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.risk: The iOS build has been off the App Store since 7 Oct 2026 and the appeal is unresolved, so it cannot be downloaded there again and only a self-signed IPA works; a free Apple ID signature expires after 7 days and the app stops opening until it is refreshed; the Android build does not support emergency calls and blocks calls to +86 numbers; whether Wi-Fi Calling registers depends on the carrier having enabled it; this is closed proprietary software and the licence forbids redistributing the packages, commercial use and removing branding, so keep it to lawful personal use; the Play build and the GitHub package are signed differently and cannot update each other, so export a backup before switching channels.
simhub-esim-reader-vowifi.source: GitHub maow318/simhubforum and its Releases (read 2026-11-23: 388 stars, 90 forks; README lists iOS 29.3, macOS 29.22 and Android 23.0, while Releases carry android-v23.1 from 2026-10-30 plus SIMKit.ipa and mac-v29.22) + Google Play cc.forserein.simhub.esim (read 2026-11-23: $2.99, 50+ installs, updated 2026-11-21, no ads, no in-app purchases listed, publisher SIMKIT LTD) + iTunes lookup for id6759248276 returned zero results in the us/jp/hk/gb/de/sg storefronts (the app is no longer on the App Store)

one-ai-api-key-free-10usd.regions: [Global] Sign in with an email or Google account, no card needed; the site lists no country restriction
one-ai-api-key-free-10usd.content: Signing up gives $10 of credit and one gateway key. one-ai-api-key-free-10usd.conditions: Register with Google or an email, no card. Each account gets 100 requests and 5 million tokens a day shared across the six ids. Keys can carry spend caps, model allow-lists and expiry. Your client must accept a custom base URL.

Copy the gateway API key from the console
Point your client's base URL at https://api.oneaiapikey.com/v1 (the bare domain for Anthropic format)

autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.title: [Global] AutoClip open-source AI editor: long videos into shorts in one click, free under MIT (cloud models billed per use)
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.highlight: Paste a podcast, interview or lecture link and it cuts up to 10 vertical or landscape clips sized for each platform, each with cover, title, description, hashtags and a ZIP release bundle. Renders locally; 14,302 stars, MIT licensed.
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.regions: [Global] Desktop app and CLI/MCP are free and open source with no regional limits; cloud analysis and image generation are billed by the provider you choose
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.value: Free (MIT open source, cloud models paid separately)
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.content: An open-source desktop editor (MIT; 14,302 stars and 2,202 forks on 24 November 2026). Paste a long podcast, interview or course link, pick a platform, and it scores and cuts up to 10 qualifying clips sized to that platform's aspect ratio and length, listing the rest as alternates; every clip ships with cover, title, description, hashtags and a ZIP bundle. Platforms covered include Douyin, Xiaohongshu, TikTok, Reels, YouTube Shorts, Bilibili and YouTube, with interview-style or full-screen podcast layouts for vertical and the original framing for Bilibili and YouTube, following the active speaker. Cutting, framing and rendering run on your machine, and subtitles can come from the creator's file, local Whisper/SenseVoice or a cloud transcript. A CLI and an MCP server share the same pipeline. In the maintainers' own test, a 1h43m English video with subtitles produced 10 clips in 7.5 minutes for about CNY 0.09 of text-model usage.
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.conditions: The software is free and MIT licensed but runs on your own machine (the documented test used an Apple Silicon Mac). Cloud analysis, AI image generation and cloud transcription are billed by whichever provider you configure, so you supply the model keys. Only process footage you have the rights to use.
steps: Download the desktop build (Windows or macOS) from GitHub Releases or the project site
Configure the analysis model and transcription method, either local Whisper or your own cloud key
Paste the long video link, choose the target platform and layout, then run one-click clipping
Fine-tune framing and subtitles in the editor and export the ZIP release bundle
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.risk: Cloud model usage is on you, and long videos across several platforms add time and spend. Clip quality depends on the model and footage, so review framing and subtitles before publishing. The repository carries 40 open issues and releases move fast, so update older builds, and you remain responsible for footage rights and each platform's rules.
autoclip-open-source-video-clipping.source: GitHub zhouxiaoka/autoclip (read 24 November 2026: 14,302 stars, 2,202 forks, MIT, created 8 July 2025; README states the software is free while cloud models are metered, with measured runtimes and CNY costs) + GitHub Trending daily list (24 November 2026, +908 stars that day)

leaflow-free-monitoring.title: [Global] Leaflow free cloud monitoring: hosts, URL checks, alerts, SLO and a public status page with no card
leaflow-free-monitoring.highlight: The official page says host monitoring, URL checks, alerts, SLO tracking and public status pages are all free; hosts need no inbound ports because the agent reports outward, the status page can use your own domain and signup takes no card
leaflow-free-monitoring.regions: [Global] Sign up with an email on the Chinese or English site and use console.leaflow.net; the monitoring agent is x86_64 only
leaflow-free-monitoring.content: Leaflow's monitoring product page states that host monitoring, URL checks and alerts, SLO and error-budget tracking and public status pages cost nothing, and that hosts do not need to open any inbound port. The agent runs in push mode by default (the first reading usually appears within a minute) or pull mode (port 10050 must be open); templates cover CPU, memory, disk and network, systemd, Docker, Nginx, PHP-FPM, certificate expiry, S.M.A.R.T., NVIDIA GPUs, ICMP and Proxmox VE. URL checks run every 60 seconds by default and can validate status codes, body keywords, redirects and response time across multi-step sessions that share a session. Status pages can be bound to your own domain, and the vendor's launch post on NodeLoc adds that DNS and the Fleet machine fleet are not charged separately and that signup needs no card.
leaflow-free-monitoring.conditions: Register a Leaflow account; the monitoring agent supports only x86_64 machines on Debian 13+ or Ubuntu 24.04+; pull mode needs port 10050 open; the free-tier limits are not published.
steps: Sign up at leaflow.net without a card and open console.leaflow.net
Register the host under monitoring, choose push mode and run the generated agent command on the machine
Tick the templates for what the machine actually runs (Docker, Nginx, GPU and so on)
Add URL checks and alert recipients, then bind your own domain if the status page should be public
leaflow-free-monitoring.risk: A free SaaS from a mainland Chinese vendor whose free-tier limits and long-term policy are unpublished; Fleet's automatic sudo review is explicitly billed by model API usage, so do not enable it by default; monitoring data sits with the vendor; a machine must stay online to run the agent.
leaflow-free-monitoring.source: Leaflow official monitoring product page (read 2026-11-24: free cloud monitoring, with host monitoring, URL checks, alerts, SLO and status pages at no charge) + the vendor's launch post on NodeLoc (2026-11-22, saying Fleet, monitoring, status pages and DNS are all free and need no card)

sie-serverless-free-credits.regions: [Global] Sign in to the console with OAuth; the site lists no country restriction
sie-serverless-free-credits.value: $20 signup credits (no card) plus $500 launch credits by application
sie-serverless-free-credits.content: SIE Serverless hosts more than 20 small task-specific models, covering OCR, document-to-Markdown, reranking, sparse and multi-vector embeddings, classification, field extraction, speech to text and PII redaction, behind one API. The official launch post says a new account gets $20 with no card, worth about 530 million embedding tokens, 50,000 pages of document parsing or 10 million generated tokens, and teams can apply for $500 more in launch credits from the console. SDKs exist for Python and TypeScript along with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and integrations for LangChain, LlamaIndex and CrewAI, and the same calls move unchanged to a self-hosted SIE Cluster; the engine is open source under Apache-2.0 and self-hosting carries no licence fee.

Copy an API key, install sie-sdk and send one encode request
Apply for the $500 launch credits in the console and describe what you are building
Switch models per task (OCR, embeddings, reranking) and note that usage is billed only after the credits run out
sie-serverless-free-credits.risk: The vendor publishes neither the expiry nor the eligible countries for the $20 and $500 credits; the $500 needs manual review with unpublished criteria and volume; usage is billed after the credits, so set a budget before batch jobs; the published benchmarks are the vendor's own, and small models trail large ones on complex reasoning; direct access from mainland China is untested.

klistra-free-350-credits.highlight: Spec-driven video: describe the scenes in a written specification and a builder agent renders it, so a change touches only what changed and the same spec re-lays out for every size; the free 350 credits cover a 15-20 second video, with no card and only the first 200 accounts
klistra-free-350-credits.regions: [Global] Sign up on the site; no card is needed and no country restriction is listed
klistra-free-350-credits.value: 350 credits (about $12-17, enough for one 15-20 second video)
klistra-free-350-credits.content: Klistra is a one-developer AI motion design and video studio: you write a scene-by-scene specification, then a builder agent renders it, and an edit changes only the part of the spec that moved. Everything is billed in credits, with a first version costing about 50-150, a round of changes 20-150, rendering 15 seconds in three sizes 2-5, a generated clip 15-60, and a picture, voiceover or music track 1-5. The free plan gives 350 credits, enough for one 15-20 second video and requires no card; Pro is $25 a month ($20 billed yearly) with 600 credits a month that roll over once, and the Claude Code integration is paid-plan only.
klistra-free-350-credits.conditions: The free plan covers only the first 200 signups and the 350 credits must be used within 60 days; no card is needed; once credits run out you buy packs from $12; the Claude Code integration is paid-plan only.
steps: Sign up at klistra.ai without a card and confirm the 350 credits land in the account
Create a project and write the scene specification (visuals, timing, assets, captions)
Render a first version, then edit only the part of the spec you want changed and render again
Export the sizes you need and use the credits within 60 days; buy a pack after that
klistra-free-350-credits.risk: Only 200 free seats exist and they opened on 18 November, so they may already be gone; it is a one-person project with no SLA and the output quality is not independently verified; generated clips are expensive at 15-60 credits, so heavy use means buying packs; credits cannot be withdrawn; Chinese interface and Chinese copy support are unverified.
klistra-free-350-credits.source: Klistra official pricing page (read 2026-11-24: the Free plan gives 350 credits to use within 60 days for the first 200 accounts with no card; Pro is $25 a month or $20 billed yearly with 600 credits) + the Show HN launch posts (18 and 21 November 2026, where the author describes credit pricing and video costs)

together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.highlight: The model page and the pricing table both list input, cached input and output at $0: PrismML squeezed Qwen3.6 27B into ternary weights (1.71 bits per weight, about 9.4x smaller than FP16) while keeping 95% of quality, a 262K context, image input and JSON mode.
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.regions: [Global] A Together AI account and API key are enough to call the serverless endpoint; the vendor publishes no rate limit, free quota or regional restriction
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.value: $0 (free input and output for a 27B-class reasoning model)
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.content: Together AI serves PrismML's Ternary Bonsai 27B on serverless inference with input, cached input and output all priced Free under the model ID Prism-ML/Ternary-Bonsai-27B. It is a ternary low-bit build of Qwen3.6 27B: every language weight takes one of three values with an FP16 scale per group of 128, measuring 1.71 bits per weight and roughly 9.4x smaller than FP16, and it claims 95% of the original quality (80.49 average over 15 thinking-mode benchmarks, with MATH-500 99.20, AIME 2025 90.84 and HumanEval+ 93.90). It carries a 262K context, a 4-bit vision tower for images and documents, JSON mode and tool calling, with recommended temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95 and top_k 20. Other models on the same platform are billed by usage (GLM-5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens).
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.conditions: Create a Together AI account and API key (endpoint Prism-ML/Ternary-Bonsai-27B) and call it through the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions route; the vendor publishes no free quota, rate limit or end date, so terms can change.
steps: Sign up at together.ai and create an API key
Send requests to https://api.together.ai/v1/chat/completions with model Prism-ML/Ternary-Bonsai-27B
Load long documents or repositories straight into the 262K context and turn on JSON mode for structured output
Test the free tier's rate limit before relying on it and keep a paid model as a fallback
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.risk: The free price comes with no end date, quota or rate limit published, so the platform can change or withdraw it; ternary quantisation still loses about 5% quality, so verify complex maths and long chains yourself; free serverless capacity is shared and queues at peak; do not put the free tier on a critical production path.
together-ternary-bonsai-27b-free.source: Together AI official model page (read 2026-11-24: Free input and output per 1M tokens, 262K context, vision and JSON, endpoint Prism-ML/Ternary-Bonsai-27B, released 2026-07-14, 99.9% SLA serverless) + the serverless table on the official pricing page (Ternary Bonsai 27B input Free, output Free, cached Free)

nebius-builder-program-credits.value: $125 of credit ($25 AI Cloud + $25 Token Factory + $25 Tavily + $50 Toloka)
nebius-builder-program-credits.content: The Nebius AI Builder Program is free to join. Its page lists $25 of AI Cloud credit (enough for an H100 for up to a day or a B300 for an afternoon at Spot prices), $25 of Token Factory credit, $25 of Tavily real-time search credit and $50 of Toloka evaluation credit, plus a $1 NVIDIA x Nebius certification, a free Agentic AI course, office hours and a Discord community. Section C.1 of the service terms says verification issues credit codes for $25 Token Factory and $25 Tavily, and C.2 makes all promotional credits non-transferable and valid for 90 days from issuance; AI Cloud and Toloka credit follow their own terms and eligibility. Registration with disposable email domains is blocked, signups are limited to one per IP per 24 hours, and credits may only be used for prototyping, experimentation and learning rather than production or revenue work; an account using more than 30% above its allocation may be auto-paused.
nebius-builder-program-credits.conditions: Register with name, email, company or university, role, country and a description of what you are building, then complete double opt-in verification; one account per verified email and one signup per IP per 24 hours; credits expire after 90 days and are limited to prototyping and experimentation; personal emails may go to manual review.
steps: Fill in the form at dev.nebius.com/builders with your name, email, company or university, role, country and project
Click the verification email so membership becomes active
Claim the Token Factory, Tavily and other credit codes and redeem them on each platform, taking AI Cloud credit when you need GPUs
Spend them within 90 days, then move to pay-as-you-go if you want to continue
nebius-builder-program-credits.risk: The terms only promise Token Factory and Tavily credit at registration, while AI Cloud and Toloka are subject to separate eligibility; personal email addresses may be reviewed and disposable ones are refused; credit expires in 90 days and is limited to prototyping, so production or revenue use breaks the terms; spending more than 30% above the allocation can trigger an automatic pause, so set limits before calling the APIs.
nebius-builder-program-credits.source: Nebius official Builder Program page (read 2026-11-24: free to join, $25 AI Cloud, $25 Token Factory, $25 Tavily, $50 Toloka, $1 certification, free course and office hours) + the official service-specific terms (C.1 issues $25 Token Factory and $25 Tavily codes after verification; C.2 90-day expiry and no transfer; H.2 bans duplicate accounts and production use)
